sense: in at one side and out at the other

evidence: Cato Agr. 76: cāseumque per crībrum facitō trānseat
terms.comment: Through a thing and out the other side, or through a space: per crībrum, through a sieve; per fenestram, through the window; per āëra, through the air. Of a person through whom: per tē, through you, thanks to you.
Verbs often say “through” themselves: perfodere, dig through; perrumpere, break through; trānsfīgere, run through, pierce.

phrases.latin: deinde crībrum farīnārium pūrum sūmitō cāseumque per crībrum facitō trānseat in mortārium
phrases.english: then take a clean flour sieve and make the cheese go through it into the mortar

phrases.latin: fōns orītur in monte, per saxa dēcurrit
phrases.english: a spring rises in the mountain and runs down through the rocks

phrases.latin: volat ille per āëra magnum rēmigiō ālārum
phrases.english: he flies through the great air, rowing with his wings

phrases.latin: at liquidī fontēs et stagna virentia muscō adsint et tenuis fugiēns per grāmina rīvus
phrases.english: but let there be clear springs and pools green with moss, and a thin stream slipping away through the grass
